provenance.citation: Fikes, R. E., & Nilsson, N. J. (1971). STRIPS: A new approach to the application of theorem proving to problem solving. Artificial Intelligence, 2(3–4), 189–208.
provenance.locus: Section 2 (p. 191) — world model, goal G, and operators O1..On; ground (Skolemised) encoding of the Section 3 room-navigation domain.
provenance.notes: The STRIPS breed engine matches premise strings exactly against the state atom set (pred=val encoding). Parametric operators require Skolemisation to ground instances before the engine can apply them. This fixture uses a two-goal room-navigation problem: robot must turn on the light (light=off → light=on) and close door1 (door1=open → door1=closed). Both operators are immediately applicable in the initial state, giving a 2-step plan within depth 16. Goals are ordered: light=on first, then door1=closed. The engine picks the first unsatisfied goal, finds an applicable operator that adds it, applies it, and recurses — matching the forward-search semantics of Fikes & Nilsson Section 2.

input.intent: turn on the light and close door1

expected.note: A 2-step plan. Each operator is directly applicable in the state where it is tried; no subgoal chaining is needed. This validates the core STRIPS forward-search loop (Fikes & Nilsson 1971, Section 2).
